criterion: Each is pinned by a named test and a mutation-audit entry, and the claims about what the existing tests guard are corrected where they were too strong
summary: Eight doctor guards, all reported pinned, and the full audit reports '45 of 45 guards pinned by their named test; 0 declared uncovered' - the audit's own output, not arithmetic. Two corrections to my own claims. First, the reviewer showed my statement that two tests were vacuous was too strong in the other direction: reverting the whole block to the read_text that shipped makes the pipe test fail on a timeout in 60.18s, so it does separate HEAD from what shipped and only fails to separate this line from a non-blocking open of the same file. The guard comment says that now. Second, the audit found a sixth vacuous test of mine while I was fixing the fifth: doctor's fixture runs graphctl init, which writes a record and creates the journal, so no test driven through doctor can reach a journal that does not exist - that arm moved to tests.test_journal_contract.SkippedMonthTests, asking the function directly, and the doctor-level test now says why it cannot hold it. Suites: 429 tests OK on 3.12.12 and 429 OK on 3.10.19; black and mypy clean over 37 files; sync_adapters --check passes.
